definition: Voice computing is the discipline that develops hardware or software to process voice inputs.
details: It spans many other fields including human-computer interaction, conversational computing, linguistics, natural language processing, automatic speech recognition, speech synthesis, audio engineering, digital signal processing, cloud computing, data science, ethics, law, and information security. Voice computing has become increasingly significant in modern times, especially with the advent of smart speakers like the Amazon Echo and Google Assistant, a shift towards serverless computing, and improved accuracy of speech recognition and text-to-speech models.

explainer.lead: Voice computing is the discipline that develops hardware or software to process voice inputs. It matters because it spans the many fields needed to build voice interfaces, now prominent through smart speakers.

tiers.eli5: It's the whole field of making machines that listen to and work with your voice.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers draw on speech recognition, synthesis, signal processing and more to build voice systems; the breadth means practitioners must coordinate many specialties, including ethics, law and security.
tiers.paperLevel: It is defined as the discipline developing hardware or software to process voice inputs, spanning human-computer interaction, linguistics, NLP, ASR, speech synthesis, DSP, cloud computing, data science, ethics, law and information security.

explainer.example: Building a smart speaker requires combining ASR, speech synthesis and cloud computing under voice computing.
